agree.reason: The open acknowledgement of Eastside and the concrete $85-to-$170 doubling give a lapsed, aggrieved donor a reason to return, but the apology is brief, says nothing about where the lessons will happen, and may not win over someone who is still angry.

honest.reason: The email correctly drops the brief's unsupported promise to place all 61 children and its arithmetic checks out, though 'every child we fund starts in January' and 'it comes to me' are small assertions the brief doesn't strictly supply.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out sensible figures ($85 to $170, $575 doubled to a full year, a full match funding 26 children), but it never sets the $15,000 match against last year's $1,240 or states the $70,150 needed for all 61 children.

right_comparison.reason: It never says what happens without a gift (children stay on the list, the match goes unused) and offers the 26-child full-match case as the benchmark when last year's response suggests the real figure is closer to two.

qualification.reason: The 'can't promise all 61' hedge plus the December 31 deadline and $15,000 cap are concrete and checkable, but the email doesn't say what happens to the match or the waiting children if the deadline is missed.

objections.reason: It meets the Eastside grievance head-on and invites replies, but it doesn't say whether the subsidized lessons will reach the families Eastside served, so the reader's core objection is only half answered.

fit.reason: It's a year-end email of about 230 words with a subject line, a clear call to give and the executive director's signature, as the brief asked.
